concept: The whole innings is one lopsided split, so the post is built on it: the hero greys out the collapse (70 for 5) and puts the final total in white, with 293 against 55 as the two facts underneath. Slide 2 turns the 368 into bars, where Nicholls and Phillips are two long bars and nine batters together make one short one. Cricket blue, type and data only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
Nine New Zealand batters made 55 between them. Two made 293.

New Zealand were 70 for 5 on day 1 at the Basin Reserve. They were bowled out for 368 on day 2.

Henry Nicholls finished 175 not out. Glenn Phillips made 118 and the pair put on 216 for the sixth wicket before Akash Deep hit the top of Phillips' off stump.

India's quicks took all 10 wickets. Jasprit Bumrah 4 for 92, Akash Deep 3 for 53, Anshul Kamboj 2 for 69 and Prasidh Krishna 1 for 100. The problem was one stand that India could not break for nearly 66 overs.

Was it the stand, or did India run out of plans? Tell us below.
